name: ALdataset
description: Active learning (AL) is a subfield of machine learning (ML) in which a learning algorithm could achieve good accuracy with less training samples by interactively querying a user/oracle to label new data points. Pool-based AL is well-motivated in many ML tasks, where unlabeled data is abundant, but their labels are hard to obtain. Although many pool-based AL methods have been developed, the lack of a comparative benchmarking and integration of techniques makes it difficult to: 1) determine the current state-of-the-art technique; 2) evaluate the relative benefit of new methods for various properties of the dataset; 3) understand what specific problems merit greater attention; and 4) measure the progress of the field over time. To conduct easier comparative evaluation among AL methods, we present a benchmark task for pool-based active learning, which consists of benchmarking datasets and quantitative metrics that summarize overall performance. We present experiment results for various active learning strategies, both recently proposed and classic highly-cited methods, and draw insights from the results.
general_score_metric: area_under_learning_curve (AULC) / accuracy at fixed labeling budgets
reputation: Well-regarded in the active learning research community as a standard suite for comparing pool-based AL strategies across datasets.
notes: Performance strongly depends on dataset properties and label budget; results sensitive to randomness and implementation details; not an LLM benchmark.
